pipeline.stages: crawl -> parse -> ocr -> parse --only-failed -> load_pg -> entities -> identity -> entities -> marts -> geo -> export -> tiles
pipeline.logs: data/logs/<stage>-<timestamp>.log; `make status` summarises; every stage records a pipeline_run row

sources.what: licensed full-power and Class A stations: call sign, community, transmitter, licensee, application IDs

sources.what: predicted F(50,90) service contours, 360 points per station, updated daily

sources.what: federal candidates and committees for the cycle, used to resolve buyer identity

modules.crawl:
Crawl FCC political files for stations into SQLite, optionally downloading PDFs.

  python3 -m ingest.crawl --stations 33710,66221 --years 2026 --download --workers 6
  python3 -m ingest.crawl --stations-file data/crawl_targets_2026.txt --state PA --years 2026 --download

Resumable and idempotent:
  * a station-year is re-listed unless its `listing` row is complete (a walk that died mid-way
    is recorded as partial and redone on the next run; --relist forces it);
  * downloads go to <file>.pdf.part and are renamed only after the PDF header/trailer check,
    so a killed run never leaves a half file that looks done; files on disk but not marked
    downloaded are verified and adopted;
  * every download failure is recorded on the file (download_attempts, download_error) and
    retried on later runs until MAX_ATTEMPTS, then reported by ingest.status as given up.
Logs to data/logs/crawl-<ts>.log; exits non-zero if failures exceed the threshold.
modules.update:
Incremental updater: apply the FCC file-history change feed to the local store.

The feed (`/api/manager/file/history.json`) lists every file added, deleted,
moved, renamed or purged across all stations for a date range, with the folder
path, size and timestamps. One call per 500 rows; a peak day is ~30 pages.

  python3 -m ingest.update                       # from last sync (or yesterday) to today
  python3 -m ingest.update --since 2026-10-20    # explicit window
  python3 -m ingest.update --download            # and fetch the new files

Only tracked stations (those already in `files`) are applied unless --stations
adds more. Re-running a window is idempotent. A day whose feed could not be read
is recorded as a failure and the sync marker is not advanced past it, so the next
run picks it up again.
modules.ocr:
OCR image-only PDFs (Nexstar, Sinclair, Gray and others file scans/prints with no text layer).

Engines
  vision     Apple Vision via the `ocrmac` package (default on macOS). ~0.2 s/page at scale 1.5 in one
             process, about 5x tesseract, with the same parse results on WideOrbit/Katz prints.
  tesseract  the tesseract CLI, psm 6, scale 2.2 (~1 s/page). Fallback / non-Mac.
Text is cached at data/ocr/<file_manager_id>.txt (pages separated by form feeds) and picked up by
ingest.parse. Each attempt is recorded in the SQLite `ocr` table; a failure is retried on later runs
until OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS and then left alone (ingest.status lists them), never retried forever.

  python3 -m ingest.ocr --workers 6                 # everything downloaded that parsed as image-only
  python3 -m ingest.ocr --engine tesseract --ids a,b
  python3 -m ingest.ocr --pages 4                   # cap pages per document (default 12)
modules.parse:
Parse downloaded political-file PDFs into structured rows.

Every document gets a kind (order | invoice | form | other), a template naming the layout that
was recognised, a source (text layer or OCR) and a parse_status (ok | partial | failed | unrecognized). Layouts:

  wideorbit-contract      WideOrbit "CONTRACT" print, text layer (Hearst, Tegna, Fox, Nexstar invoices...)
  wideorbit-contract-ocr  the same printed to an image PDF and OCR'd (Nexstar, Gray)
  wideorbit-order         WideOrbit "ORDER" print ("Order / Rev:", "Flight Dates:"), text (Gray, Nexstar, Scripps, Allen)
  wideorbit-order-ocr     the same OCR'd (Gray scans)
  wideorbit-invoice       WideOrbit invoice with per-spot Ad-ID lines
  katz                    Katz / Sinclair contract ("Contract #", "Total $:"), text or OCR
  katz-ecr                Katz ECR confirmation contract ("External #", "Grand Total:"), Sinclair stations
  locality-worksheet      Locality rep "CONTRACT WORKSHEET REPORT" (OCR)
  sinclair-contract       Sinclair traffic contract ("Contract #", "Date Entered", "Schedule Dates"), OCR
  eport                   Sinclair ePort order/revision summary
  sinclair-invoice        Sinclair "OFFICIAL BILLING INVOICE" (text or OCR)
  nab-acroform            NAB PB-19 fillable form, values in AcroForm fields
  nab-text                NAB / station agreement forms read from page text or OCR (scanned, signed forms)
  nab-supplement          ad-specific NAB supplements and addenda (ISCI codes, no money) -> kind other
Anything else is kind=other with template NULL so the gap is visible; ingest.validate clusters those.

Text extraction is cached under data/text/<ab>/<file_id>.json (text layer, AcroForm fields, page count) so
re-parsing after a parser change is regex-only. Image-only PDFs are flagged needs_ocr; ingest.ocr fills
data/ocr/<file_id>.txt and `parse --only-failed` picks the text up.

  python3 -m ingest.parse                 # parse everything downloaded and not yet at PARSER_VERSION
  python3 -m ingest.parse --only-failed   # re-parse documents that are not ok or unrecognised (after OCR)
  python3 -m ingest.parse --reparse       # everything (from the text cache)
  python3 -m ingest.parse --file x.pdf    # print the parse of one file
modules.validate:
Parse validation report: invariants checked over document.raw in Postgres, failure rates per template,
and the worst examples with file ids so a human can open the PDFs.

Checks (each applies only where the fields exist):
  lines_sum          order line amounts sum to the order gross (WideOrbit prints with line items)
  net_ratio          net is gross less the 15% agency commission (or equal to gross for direct buys)
  order_no_filename  a 7-9 digit number in the station's file name, when present, matches the parsed order number
  flight_range       flight dates fall inside the cycle window and start <= end
  gross_range        gross is between 0 and $5M (orders above $2M are listed for eyeballing)
  invoice_spots      WideOrbit invoice 'Total Spots' equals the number of per-spot lines read
  invoice_linked     an invoice's order number matches an order filed by the same station
  form_fields        a form yields an advertiser (committee / candidate / sponsor)
  dup_order_cross    an order number appears at stations of different groups (same group = sister stations, normal)

  python3 -m ingest.validate                   # full report
  python3 -m ingest.validate --examples 12     # more worst examples per check
  python3 -m ingest.validate --json > report.json
Also prints parse coverage by kind / template / status, which is the before/after number for parser work.
modules.load_pg:
Load stations (web/data/stations.json) and the crawl store (data/political.sqlite) into Postgres.

Idempotent: rows are upserted by primary key. Run after every crawl/parse.
  python3 -m ingest.load_pg [--db data/political.sqlite]

station_group is derived from the licensee string with the rules in GROUPS (checked against every licensee
in the station table: the large groups use dozens of licensee entities, e.g. Sinclair's "<CALL> Licensee, LLC",
Allen Media's "<City> TV License Company, LLC", Tegna's legacy Belo/Gannett companies). Stations no rule
matches get "Independent", public and religious broadcasters are grouped as such; NULL means unknown.
modules.entities:
Rebuild domain entities from `document.raw` + `opif_file.folder_path`.

Deterministic and total: it truncates the entity tables and rebuilds them, so a parser
improvement or an alias change only needs `load_pg` + `entities`, never a recrawl.
Manual buyer merges live in data/buyer_overrides.yaml (alias -> canonical name) and are
applied on top of the automatic folder-based identity.
  python3 -m ingest.entities
modules.identity:
Buyer identity: merge the stations' own folder labels into canonical buyers and match them
to FEC candidates and committees.

Inputs: buyer_alias rows of source 'folder' (one per station label) with the station's state,
FEC bulk master files in data/fec (cn.txt candidates, cm.txt committees, ccl.txt linkage),
and data/buyer_overrides.yaml (manual: `raw label: Canonical Name`, or `category|raw label: ...`).
Output: data/buyer_identity.json, read by ingest.entities on its next run.

  python3 -m ingest.identity          # then: python3 -m ingest.entities
modules.geo:
Geography: counties with population, H3 cells with population, and station coverage shares.

  python3 -m ingest.geo            # everything (downloads Census files to data/geo on first run)

Resolutions come from HEX_RES. Coarse resolutions are built nationwide; fine ones only inside
the contours of stations that have political files loaded ("active"), so the fine layers grow
with the crawl. Adding a resolution is a one-line change here plus a rerun.
modules.export:
Export serving artifacts from the marts.

web/data/spend/<facility>.json, index.json   per-station buyers (what the map reads today)
web/data/hex/total_r<res>.json                money/ads reaching each cell (for the hex layers)
data/marts/*.parquet                          every mart, for DuckDB / the next UI / analysis
web/data/build.json                           build id + timestamp (cache busting)

python3 -m ingest.export
modules.tiles:
Vector tiles (PMTiles) for the map: hex money layers and station contours, via tippecanoe.

python3 -m ingest.tiles        -> web/data/tiles/hex5.pmtiles, hex7.pmtiles, contours.pmtiles, meta.json
modules.places:
Static place index for search: ZIP centroids and populated places from the Census Gazetteer files.
Writes web/data/places.json so the app can resolve "50309", "Des Moines" or "Des Moines, IA" with no
external geocoder. Street addresses still fall back to Nominatim in the app.

  python3 -m ingest.places
modules.status:
Pipeline status: what has been listed, downloaded, OCR'd, parsed and loaded, per station and overall,
which stages are running or failed last, and what is stuck.

  python3 -m ingest.status                 # overall + per-stage last runs + problem list
  python3 -m ingest.status --stations      # add a per-station table (sorted by pending work)
  python3 -m ingest.status --state PA      # per-station table for one state
  python3 -m ingest.status --json          # machine-readable (used by ingest.batch and the About page export)
Reads SQLite only (never blocks a running stage: WAL mode) plus the lock files; Postgres counts are
included when it is reachable.
modules.coverage:
Coverage report: what has been crawled versus the national political-file totals.

The denominator is data/political_doc_counts.csv: per-station document counts for 2024 and 2026 for all
1,750 licensed full-power stations (one FCC folder call each, taken 2026-10-23). The numerator is the
local store (files listed, downloaded, parsed ok). Reported per state and per year, plus the gap list.

  python3 -m ingest.coverage              # table by state
  python3 -m ingest.coverage --json       # for export_methods / the About page
  python3 -m ingest.coverage --missing    # stations not yet crawled, biggest first
modules.batch:
National crawl driver: one state at a time, crawl -> parse -> OCR -> parse, with the Postgres refresh
(load_pg, entities, identity, entities, marts) running in the background after each state while the next
state downloads. Holds the "pipeline" lock so two drivers cannot overlap.

  python3 -m ingest.batch --targets data/crawl_targets_2026_national.txt --years 2026
  python3 -m ingest.batch ... --states TX,OH          # a subset, in that order
  python3 -m ingest.batch ... --all                   # redo states already marked done (cheap: crawl skips complete listings)

Resumable: each state that finishes crawl+parse+ocr+parse gets a pipeline_run row (stage=batch_state, batch=<ST>,
status ok); a rerun skips those unless --all. A state whose crawl fails is recorded failed and the driver moves on;
three consecutive failed states abort the run (the FCC edge is refusing us). Monitor with `make status` or
`tail -f data/logs/batch-*.log`; every stage keeps its own log in data/logs/.
modules.runlog:
Run bookkeeping shared by every pipeline stage: log files, locks, counts, and the pipeline_run table.

    from .runlog import Stage
    with Stage("crawl", args=vars(a), db_path=a.db) as st:
        st.count("listed", n)
        st.fail(file_id, "HTTP 404")       # logged with the id and reason, counted, summarised
        ...
    # on exit: SUMMARY line, pipeline_run row closed, exit 1 if the stage failed or
    # failures exceeded max_fail_rate of the work attempted

Every stage writes data/logs/<stage>-<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.log (INFO and above) and mirrors it to stderr.
A per-stage lock in data/locks/ stops two instances of the same stage from overlapping; the batch
driver (ingest.batch) additionally holds the "pipeline" lock so two full pipeline runs cannot overlap.
Stage runs are recorded in the SQLite pipeline_run table (copied to Postgres by load_pg), with start,
end, status, counts and the log path, so `ingest.status` can show what ran and what failed last.
